nodes.title: Hold one request state object
nodes.why: Loading, ready, empty and error are one question with one answer at a time. A tagged union makes the screen derive from it, and the keepRows flag tells a first load from a refresh.
nodes.alternative: Keep separate loading, error and empty booleans.
nodes.tradeoff: Separate flags are quicker to add but can all be true at once after a fast sequence of requests; the union cannot.

nodes.title: Number every request and compare when it settles
nodes.why: A source change while a request is running makes the old answer wrong. The ref holds the newest number, and a response that carries an older one returns without touching state.
nodes.alternative: Flip a cancelled flag in the effect cleanup.
nodes.tradeoff: A flag covers the effect but not the refresh handler; one counter in a ref covers both paths with the same check.

nodes.title: Treat a refresh differently from a first load
nodes.why: A first load has nothing to show, so clearing is right. A refresh already has rows worth keeping, so the loading and error states carry a keepRows flag and the table stays.
nodes.alternative: Clear the rows at the start of every request.
nodes.tradeoff: Clearing is simpler and makes the table flash on every refresh; keeping the rows needs the flag but matches what the tester asked for.

nodes.title: Narrow the payload with type guards
nodes.why: The export is unknown until each field is checked. A guard per field keeps the well-formed records, counts the rest and gives the component a real Delivery array.
nodes.alternative: Cast the payload to Delivery[] and let the table render whatever arrives.
nodes.tradeoff: A cast compiles and renders eleven legacy rows, five of them broken in a different field each; narrowing costs a loop and shows six rows and the skipped count.

nodes.title: Read the current source in the refresh handler
nodes.why: The reported bug was a useCallback with an empty dependency list: it captured the first source and reloaded the live export forever. A plain handler reads the state of the current render.
nodes.alternative: Keep useCallback and list source in its dependencies.
nodes.tradeoff: Both fix the bug; the dependency list is right when a memoized child needs a stable handler, and nothing here does.

nodes.title: Update the retried row with functional setState
nodes.why: The row turns pending before the call answers and delivered when it does. Both updates map over the current rows and merge only the fields the call changed, so a second retry or a refresh in between is never undone; a failed call puts the row back to failed.
nodes.alternative: Set a copy of the rows captured when the button was clicked.
nodes.tradeoff: The captured copy is easier to read but loses any change made during the 200 ms call: two quick retries leave the first row stuck at pending.

nodes.title: Derive the visible rows from the filter
nodes.why: The filter is a view over the rows, not a second list. Deriving it means a retry, a refresh and a filter change can never disagree, and the count line reads both lengths.
nodes.alternative: Filter the rows into a second state array when the select changes.
nodes.tradeoff: A second array renders once with stale rows after every retry or refresh; the memo recomputes only when the rows or the filter change.
